source.product: No real product. An invented generic Japandi bouclé ottoman pouf created for the hackathon demo catalogue; it does not depict or reproduce any manufacturer's design, and its price is invented demo data.
source.generation: Four-view turnaround reference sheet generated with the codex-image skill (front, three-quarter-front-left, side profile, rear on a seamless white studio backdrop), cut into four images with scripts/turnaround_crop.mjs, then Higgsfield generate_3d model multi_image_to_3d with all four views as role "image": should_texture=true, enable_pbr=true, should_remesh=true, topology=triangle, target_polycount=30000, symmetry_mode=auto, rigging and animation false, plus a texture_prompt describing cream bouclé looped pile and pale oak feet.
source.postProcessing: npx @gltf-transform/cli resize --width 1024 --height 1024 (textures only, geometry untouched; 14.01 MB -> 3.66 MB), then scripts/fit_glb.py 60 60 42 to centre the footprint, put the base at y=0 and scale to the listing size.

knownLimitations: Dimensions are a visual proxy, not a measured product, but this asset happens to fit exactly: 60.0 x 60.0 x 42.0 cm against the intended 60 x 60 x 42 cm, with 4.01% anisotropy, well inside the 10% cap. fit_glb.py exited 0.

Because the piece is near-symmetrical the four reference views were nearly identical, so the reconstruction had little independent information about the rear; the sides are plausible rather than derived.
The bouclé reads slightly whiter than the intended #f1ece2 cream.
The silhouette came out rounder and more barrel-like than a square-cornered pouf; it reads as a soft drum pouf with a seam around the circumference.
Reconstructed from generated reference images, not from photographs of a real object.

No manual Blender inspection or correction pass has been done. Verified by rendering the GLB in model-viewer from front, rear three-quarter and low angles; geometry and the four oak feet are clean, with no holes or floating fragments and no dark underside cap.
